Article Title: Oil prices slip over $1 as US weighs ‘D-Day’ Iran sanctions; Strait of Hormuz shipping risks in focus
Article Text:
Oil prices slip over $1 per barrel

US threatens wider economic pressure

Iran warns of oil export halt

Oil prices eased more than $1 a barrel on Monday as investors booked profits ahead of a US announcement on new sanctions against Iran, with markets weighing the possibility of further disruption to Middle Eastern supplies.Brent crude declined 1.90% to $92.60 a barrel while WTI crude fell 1.96% to $85.35 per barrel, as of 7:30 am IST.The decline came after both benchmarks gained more than 5% last week, marking their second consecutive weekly rises. The gains followed a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks, which had contributed to a sharp reduction in oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz. The waterway had previously carried a fifth of the world's oil supply.The latest focus is on Washington's planned sanctions. US treasury decretary Scott Bessent is scheduled to hold a press conference at 2 pm EDT (1800 GMT) on Monday and has warned of "the toughest sanctions in history" against Iran. US President Donald Trump has also threatened measures against countries trading with Tehran."But if the US measures do work as intended, Iran's ability to respond via increased violence becomes a growing risk for energy markets to consider."Iran has rejected the planned sanctions, while President Masoud Pezeshkian has called for a diplomatic resolution.The impact is already being felt in the country's oil trade. Trade sources cited by Reuters said that offers of Iranian crude to Chinese buyers had fallen and prices had risen after a US blockade reduced Tehran's shipments.At the same time, Iran allowed several Iraqi oil tankers to travel through the Strait of Hormuz after repeated requests from Baghdad, according to Iran's state news agency IRNA.Washington has described the coming measures as "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled", with Iran's trading partners among those expected to be targeted.Iran has responded by threatening to halt all oil exports from the Gulf if the economic pressure continues.Bessent is expected to outline the measures during Monday's press conference, as Washington steps up economic pressure on a country that has faced almost continuous sanctions since the 1979 Islamic Revolution."At dawn begins an economic D-Day — the single greatest financial offensive ever marshalled against an adversary," Bessent wrote in an opinion piece published in the Financial Times on Sunday.He has also warned countries maintaining economic and financial ties with Iran about the consequences of continuing those relationships, without specifying the measures Washington plans to impose."They would do well to consider the consequences of sustaining it," he wrote in the Financial Times.China has also been urged by Bessent to cooperate with the US, particularly as half of its oil imports from the Gulf region come from the region. China's embassy in Washington said "sanctions and pressure do not help resolve the problem," while calling for diplomacy.Iran has spent days preparing for the new sanctions and has issued increasingly strong warnings over its possible response.Earlier on Sunday, Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, said that Tehran could respond economically if the pressure continued."If the economic war continues, not a single drop of oil will be exported, neither through the Strait of Hormuz nor from anywhere in the Persian Gulf," Rezaei wrote in a social media post."Iran will regard any country’s participation in or support for America’s economic war against the Iranian people as an act of war."Iran's ability to disrupt energy supplies remains a major concern for oil markets. The country has retained enough missile and drone capability to threaten Gulf neighbours and oil tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, while shipping through the waterway has been brought close to a standstill.The condition of Iran's nuclear programme remains unknown, while the US and Israel have sought to destroy it.Meanwhile, oil prices have remained volatile as the conflict continues to rage. However, the latest spike is far below the $126 a barrel level seen earlier in the conflict.
Article Summary: Brent crude down 1.90% to $92.60 a barrel, while WTI crude falls 1.96%. Both benchmarks gained more than 5% last week, marking their second consecutive weekly rises. The gains followed a stalemate in US-Iran peace talks, which contributed to a sharp reduction in oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.

Article Title: KPMG Australia to cut 5% of workforce amid scandal, weak growth outlook
Article Text:
KPMG Australia to cut 5% of workforce amid scandal, weak growth outlook

Revenue falls as consulting business takes hit

Government scrutiny intensifies

KPMG Australia is reducing its workforce by about 5% as the firm continues to deal with the fallout from a scandal involving confidential client information and faces a subdued economic outlook.The cuts will affect 27 partners and about 360 employees, with consulting and business services expected to account for most of the reduction.The move comes as the firm undergoes a leadership overhaul following allegations that staff used inside information to secure lucrative audit contracts. The allegations were made by whistleblowers in March and have since brought KPMG Australia under intense scrutiny from the Australian government and major corporate clients.John Sams, who became KPMG Australia's CEO last month, acknowledged the challenges that the firm is facing."We recognise the challenges created by our own failings, and the work we must continue ⁠to do to rebuild trust," Sams said in a statement cited by Reuters .KPMG Australia said it expected economic growth to remain subdued until at least 2028. It said this would weigh on client investment and result in longer decision-making timeframes."While these conditions are likely to persist, we remain focused ⁠on what we can control," Sams said.The firm's revenue fell 1% to $1.6 billion in the year ended June 2026. Consulting revenue dropped 17%, with the loss of government contracts contributing to the decline.However, four of KPMG Australia's five divisions recorded higher revenue during the year. Deal advisory and infrastructure revenue increased 3%, while tax and legal, and audit and assurance each recorded 11% growth. Revenue in the mid-market and private division rose 6.4%.Average pay for equity partners declined 13% during the year as KPMG dealt with the impact of the scandal and reviewed its costs.The controversy has also resulted in several senior departures, including the firm's former CEO, audit boss and chairman, as well as senior audit partners.KPMG Australia has agreed not to bid for new federal government work until September 30. The Australian government said in June that reviews into the firm's governance, culture, ethics and integrity were underway.The latest developments come as the government considers wider changes to the country's accounting sector. Last month, it said it was considering breaking up the Big Four: KPMG, Deloitte, EY and PwC.The firms currently operate as partnerships rather than companies and are therefore not subject to supervision by Australia's corporate regulator. That arrangement could change under reforms being considered by the government.The sector has faced a series of controversies in recent years. A tax leaks scandal at PwC in 2023 prompted parliamentary inquiries, although most of the recommendations have yet to be implemented.Alongside the workforce reduction, KPMG Australia said it planned to simplify parts of its structure, with the aim of creating more integrated teams and aligning them more closely with its global advisory services.
Article Summary: KPMG Australia to cut 5% of workforce amid scandal, weak growth outlook. Firm's revenue fell 1% to $1.6 billion in the year ended June 2026. Consulting revenue dropped 17%, with loss of government contracts contributing to decline.

Article Title: Shriram bullish on CV growth despite recent price hikes
Article Text:
Shriram Finance sees strong CV demand despite price hikes, while EV financing jumps fivefold to Rs 250 crore monthly

MUMBAI: Price hikes in commercial vehicles are unlikely to dent demand, according to Shriram Finance (SFL), the largest financier of CVs, in the wake of commodity inflation-driven price hikes.SFL is also seeing a surge in electric vehicle financing with monthly disbursements having risen five-fold to Rs 250 crore this year from Rs 50 crore last year. The company expects monthly EV disbursements to rise further to Rs 500 crore next year.Speaking to TOI, Umesh Revankar, executive vice-chairman, SFL said the demand for CVs depends on economic activity and India has been able to manage both the US tariff and West Asia challenges. He added that firming prices will benefit existing vehicle owners as the value of their vehicles and freight rates rise.Higher vehicle prices also increase the value financed and support loan book growth. Revankar said the company's branch network should help it gain market share, while commercial vehicle demand showed neither stress nor unusual acceleration.Japan's MUFG's decision to buy 20% in SFL for nearly Rs 40,000 crore through a preferential issue gives Shriram Finance capital cover until 2030, Revankar said.The company plans to open about 150 branches and add 2,000-3,000 people this financial year. MUFG will also help connect SFL with Japanese companies seeking financial assistance in India.SFL expects an 18-20% growth in assets for FY27 and aims to double in five years. Electric vehicle demand has come from two-wheelers, three-wheelers and four-wheelers, while commercial vehicles are also moving steadily towards electrification.
Article Summary: Shriram Finance sees strong CV demand despite price hikes, while EV financing jumps fivefold to Rs 250 crore monthly. SFL expects an 18-20% growth in assets for FY27 and aims to double in five years. Japan's MUFG's decision to buy 20% in SFL for nearly Rs 40,000 crore gives Shriram finance capital cover until 2030.

Article Title: India eyes enhancing trade pact with Chile
Article Text:
India steps up Latin America outreach, with Chile trade pact talks and engagements with Argentina, Brazil

NEW DELHI: Amid the global turbulence, govt is stepping up its engagement with Latin America, seeking to diversify its trade basket with talks with Chile scheduled for later this week to finalise a comprehensive trade treaty.Commerce secretary Rajesh Agrawal will be in Chile as part of an effort to bridge some of the gaps related to market access and critical minerals, an official said. "The new govt in Chile is keen on the agreement. Both sides are looking to find solutions to the pending issues and there are only a few issues that need to be resolved. We are trying to move forward," the official said. India and Chile had signed a preferential trade agreement (PTA) in 2007 and are seeking to enhance the ties.Agrawal's visit coincides with engagements with Argentina and Brazil, also scheduled for later this week, and officials said that the idea is to step up trade with the region. While expansion of the PTA with Mercosur - which includes Brazil, Argentina, Uruguay, Paraguay and Bolivia - has been on the horizon, the talks are expected to focus more on bilateral issues.Latin America accounts for less than 3.5% of India's exports, which added up to $4.4 billion during the June quarter.In contrast, imports were of the order of 6.4% and were estimated at just under $14 billion.The talks come amid efforts from some of the Latin American countries to diversify their trade beyond the US and China. India too sees the region as a large market. Separately, talks are underway with Mexico to finalise the terms of reference for a PTA.
Article Summary: India steps up Latin America outreach, with Chile trade pact talks and engagements with Argentina, Brazil. India and Chile had signed a preferential trade agreement (PTA) in 2007. Separately, talks are underway with Mexico to finalise the terms of reference for a PTA.

Article Title: FPIs accelerate buying: Invest 23.5k crore in August
Article Text:
FPIs pour Rs 23,544 crore into Indian equities in August as earnings recovery and rupee stability boost investor sentiment

NEW DELHI: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have accelerated buying in Indian equities this month, infusing Rs 23,544 crore so far as improving quarterly earnings, a stable rupee and better market prospects lift sentiment.The inflow comes after FPIs invested Rs 20,200 crore in July, marking a sharp turnaround from four consecutive months of heavy selling and signalling renewed confidence in Indian equities.FPIs had withdrawn Rs 49,340 crore in June, Rs 32,963 crore in May, Rs 60,847 crore in April and a massive Rs 1.17 lakh crore in March. Prior to this selling streak, they had invested Rs 22,615 crore in Feb, according to CDSL data.Despite the recent buying, foreign investors have remained net sellers in Indian equities in 2026, withdrawing around Rs 2.3 lakh crore so far -- exceeding the Rs 1.7 lakh crore outflow registered during the entire 2025. "Factors that are driving FPIs back to India are: earnings growth revival as reflected in Q1 results, FPI withdrawal from the 'chip trade', rupee stability and the impressive growth prospects of companies in the broader market," VK Vijayakumar of Geojit Investments, said.
Article Summary: Foreign Portfolio Investors (FPIs) have accelerated buying in Indian equities this month, infusing Rs 23,544 crore. The inflow comes after FPIs invested Rs 20,200 crore in July, marking a sharp turnaround from four consecutive months of heavy selling.

Article Title: Syed Akbaruddin, Annie George Mathew, Janmejaya Kumar Sinha on RBI board
Article Text:
Centre appoints Annie George Mathew, Janmejaya Sinha and Syed Akbaruddin as part-time directors on RBI’s central board

MUMBAI: The Centre has appointed former finance ministry special secretary Annie George Mathew, Boston Consulting Group India chairman Janmejaya Kumar Sinha and former diplomat Syed Akbaruddin as part-time, non-official directors on RBI's central board for four years.The appointments committee of the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the department of financial services Aug 22, selecting the three candidates.Mathew, a Sixteenth Finance Commission member and former special secretary, expenditure, has 34 years' experience in public finance, govt audit/accounts, procurement and financial management. Sinha, who began his career at RBI, advises govt on structural reforms and economic transformation. He was a private-sector member of the Rajiv Gauba-led reform panels for Viksit Bharat 2047.Meanwhile, Akbaruddin, a 1985-batch IFS officer, was India's permanent representative to the UN from 2016-20, MEA spokesperson from 2012-15 and India's representative at IAEA from 2006-11.
Article Summary: Centre appoints Annie George Mathew, Janmejaya Sinha and Syed Akbaruddin as part-time directors on RBI’s central board. The appointments committee of the Cabinet approved the proposal made by the department of financial services Aug 22, selecting the three candidates.

Article Title: Weakness in currency can create negative loop: HSBC
Article Text:
HSBC India CEO Hitendra Dave says the bank is doubling down on affluent banking, while eyeing growth in wealth management, digital services and cross-border offerings

How did HSBC lead FCNR(B) mobilisation?

How will you deploy the rupees raised by swapping the dollars with RBI?

Will you focus only on affluent customers?

Has India lost favour among

foreign investors

?

Why has corporate capex been weak?

Are you funding acquisitions now that this is allowed?

Are large IPOs crowding out smaller players?

MUMBAI: HSBC has been in India since 1853 and has maintained the most consistent retail presence among global banks. Its Indian operations have doubled pre-tax profits in four years, making it the leading foreign bank by revenue and balance sheet, which stood at $50 billion. Hitendra Dave, HSBC India's CEO since 2021, spoke about the bank's FCNR(B) mobilisation and ambitions in affluent banking.We are the most preferred global bank among India's affluent. Our deposit mobilisation reflects our strength and reach in the NRI community across markets. Beyond FCNR(B) deposits, HSBC has helped Indian banks raise dollar resources, deploying about $1.5 billion to $2 billion through bilateral bonds and similar amounts through foreign currency loans. In the overseas bond issues by two private banks, we were practically the only bank participating, and these were large transactions.Our asset-liability management tools tell us the bucket-wise gaps we can run. Even if we park the funds in G-secs, we have a spread of 75-100 bps. We have announced fixed-rate mortgages starting at 7.5% for the initial three years, addressing buyers' concerns about rising interest rates.Our balance sheet was Rs 4.5 lakh crore at end-March and would have easily crossed Rs 5 lakh crore.Our GIFT City balance sheet would also have increased because some leverage is provided from there.Mass affluent is the entry point for acquiring affluent customers. We are doubling down on wealth and affluent banking through digital platforms, advisory services and cross-border products spanning LRS, offshore accounts, GIFT City, mortgages and premium cards.Of 20 approved branches, eight have opened, prioritising cities with high mutual fund penetration and NRI diaspora, which has helped FCNR(B) collections. We are also setting up a stockbroking arm.Financial markets are inherently short-term in their thinking. Capital chases whatever is currently selling elsewhere. There is massive debt issuance by US hyperscalers, more than by some sovereigns, while equities in Taiwan and Korea are attracting capital.Currency weakness can create a self-fulfilling negative loop, with investors holding back and weaker inflows keeping the rupee under pressure. Corporate earnings have improved after weakening a couple of years ago, but valuations have not.A spark is needed to shift the narrative, such as lower oil prices, new land or labour reforms or major FDI announcements.Capex is often viewed through the 2012-14 cycle, when mega projects in power, steel and cement had virtually no genuine promoter equity and were largely bank-financed. With little equity, promoters had less incentive to fight for or stay with projects when conditions deteriorated. We do not want such projects because they involve taxpayer money. Current growth is instead seeing capacity expansion through consolidation, with well-capitalised groups such as Tata, UltraTech and Adani expanding through internal cash flows.We are the number one bank in acquisition financing. We were the first, and at that time the only bank, to fund the two domestic M&A directly from our local-currency balance sheet.The inverse economics of asset markets means more investors enter when prices rise. Successful giant IPOs draw in new retail investors and deeper pools of international institutional capital by demonstrating that India can handle large-scale liquidity. Whether an issue performs well on listing depends on whether the issuer has maximised its valuation and pricing.
Article Summary: HSBC has been in India since 1853 and has maintained the most consistent retail presence among global banks. Its Indian operations have doubled pre-tax profits in four years. Hitendra Dave, HSBC India's CEO since 2021, spoke about the bank's FCNR(B) mobilisation.

Article Title: Government looks to deepen trade ties with Japan
Article Text:
Piyush Goyal to push India-Japan trade ties, with focus on semiconductors, AI, startups and investment

TOKYO: Commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal is set to step up the trade and investment engagement with Japan, a key strategic partner for India, especially in high-technology manufacturing and next-generation industries.Dedicated sessions are planned on semiconductors, artificial intelligence and startups, along with meetings with foreign institutional investors. In recent years, Japan has increased investment, especially in the financial services space where Mitsubishi UFJ Financial Group bought into Shriram Finance while Mizuho acquired a majority stake in Avendus.Japan and India have been seeking to strengthen their ties and take on China in areas such as lithium-ion batteries through collaborations. Last year, Japan slipped to the fifth place among global FDI investors in India, but the recent deals are expected to provide a boost.Goyal will lead a 200-member-strong industry delegation that will seek to build upon traditional ties in automobiles and steel. "The visit reflects the scale of ambition both nations bring to their special strategic and global partnership, and comes at a time when India and Japan are looking to significantly deepen trade and investment ties," an official statement said.The India-Japan trade agreement is also expected to be discussed during bilateral meetings at the ministerial level. India's bilateral trade with Japan was pegged at around $122 billion last year, with exports at $44 billion and a trade deficit of over $33 billion. Govt has been seeking a review of the trade agreement to make it more balanced in India's favour.
Article Summary: commerce and industry minister Piyush Goyal set to step up engagement with Japan. Goyal will lead a 200-member-strong industry delegation that will seek to build upon traditional ties in automobiles and steel. India-Japan trade agreement is also expected to be discussed during bilateral meetings.

Article Title: Nifty 500 companies earnings jump 13% in Q1, OMCs feel West Asia heat
Article Text:
India’s corporate earnings rebound strengthens

Telecom, metals lead the way

Broad-based growth

MUMBAI: The pace of earnings growth of the top 500 companies in the country during April-June quarter (Q1 of FY27) stood at 13% on an annual basis. But, excluding oil marketing companies, that are facing huge input cost pressures due to the war in West Asia, earnings growth was 23%, a more than two-year high, a report by Motilal Oswal Financial Services showed.Mid and small cap companies continued to outperform large caps in terms of earnings growth, although in terms of sales growth during the quarter, large caps were ahead of mid cap companies but trailed small caps.On the sectoral front, metals and financials led the quarter, while OMCs dragged sharply. "The healthy earnings growth in 1QFY27, was fuelled by a resilient macro environment, better-than-expected margin print, and improving operating conditions, which supported a strong earnings momentum. These factors further strengthened the earnings cycle from the FY25 lows," the report said.It also noted that the aggregate sales of Nifty 500 companies excluding-OMCs grew 19% YoY in Q1FY27, marking the strongest growth in 15 quarters after a prolonged period of moderate revenue growth. It also noted that earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortisation (EBITDA), again excluding-OMCs, grew 16% on the year during the quarter.On the sectoral front, the report noted that corporate earnings during April-June clocked broad-based growth, with significant contributions from metals, financials and telecom.Telecom earnings rose 384%, metals was up 57% on the year (marking the fourth consecutive quarter of strong earnings growth), while financials, led by NBFCs-lending grew 27% and banks (15%). Technology (14%) was another key contributor to the quarter's earnings. In contrast, earnings of oil & gas companies dipped 34% on the year, led by OMCs (which reported a loss of Rs 18,100 crore in Q1FY27 against a profit of Rs 16,200in Q1FY26) and cement (-1%) dragged overall earnings.Small cap companies led the Q1FY27 earnings performance of the Nifty-500, with Nifty Smallcap-250 companies reporting 35% annual growth, the report said.Nifty midcap-150 companies (ex-OMC) also delivered a strong 30% YoY growth, while largecaps (ex-OMCs) reported 20% YoY growth, the highest in 10 quarters.
Article Summary: The pace of earnings growth of the top 500 companies in the country during April-June quarter (Q1 of FY27) stood at 13% on an annual basis. But, excluding oil marketing companies, that are facing huge input cost pressures due to the war in West Asia, earnings growth was 23%, a more than two-year high.

Article Title: Cost pressure: Carmakers see strong sales but lower profits
Article Text:
Carmakers see sales surge, but rising costs squeeze profits

Higher sales fail to lift automakers’ profits as costs rise

NEW DELHI: Carmakers are selling more vehicles, but higher volumes are not necessarily translating into fatter profits. Rising commodity costs, adverse currency movements and production disruptions are squeezing margins at some of India's biggest passenger vehicle makers even as demand remains strong.Maruti Suzuki is the clearest example. Its total sales volume jumped 29.3% year-on-year to a record over 6.8 lakh units in the June quarter, while net sales rose 36% to Rs 49,959 crore. Yet net profit fell 10.8% to Rs 3,352 crore. Operating EBITDA declined 6.7% and margin contracted to 8.6% from 12.6% a year earlier."Higher volumes normally provide operating leverage. In the current environment, part of that benefit is being absorbed by higher input costs," said Ravi Bhatia, director, Jato Dynamics.Puneet Gupta, director, S&P Global Mobility, said commodity prices have moved up sharply, with copper up around 20% and aluminium around 15%, alongside higher logistics and other costs. Automakers, he said, are absorbing a significant part of these increases rather than passing them on fully to consumers to avoid disrupting sales momentum.Maruti has said material costs rose during the quarter and were aggravated by the West Asia conflict, while a temporary shift to monthly commodity settlements with suppliers as aluminium prices surged also affected margins.Tata Motors Passenger Vehicles' domestic business delivered 46% volume growth and a 64.8% rise in revenue to Rs 17,900 crore. EBITDA margin was 4.3%, though 30 basis points higher year-on-year. At the consolidated level, including Jaguar Land Rover, revenue rose 9.3% to Rs 95,799 crore while net profit plunged about 80% to Rs 775 crore, hit by JLR supply constraints, commodities and forex.Hyundai Motor India faced a sharper squeeze. Domestic volumes rose 5.4%, but exports fell 19.6%. Revenue slipped marginally to Rs 16,335 crore, while net profit declined 35% to Rs 889 crore. EBITDA margin fell to 9.3% from 13.3%."There is also a timing effect. Changes in commodity and currency costs can affect OEMs before they are recovered through vehicle pricing," Bhatia said. Realised pricing, he added, also depends on product and variant mix, discounts, dealer support and financing incentives.Gupta said the pressure is not just cyclical. Automakers are also committing significant capital to new plants and multiple powertrain technologies, including EVs, CNG and plug-in hybrids. "A lot of money is also going into capex, and that obviously eats into current profitability," he said.
Article Summary: Maruti Suzuki's total sales volume jumped 29.3% year-on-year to a record over 6.8 lakh units. Yet net profit fell 10.8% to Rs 3,352 crore. Operating EBITDA declined 6.7% and margin contracted to 8.6%.

Article Title: Onion prices surge; Centre to roll out Kanda Express from Monday
Article Text:
Centre to roll out ‘Kanda Express’ from Monday as onion prices surge 45% year-on-year

NEW DELHI: In its bid to check rising prices of onion across different regions, govt will start offloading its buffer stock. As average price of the key kitchen commodity increased to Rs 42 per kg on Saturday, 45% higher than last year and 19% more than last month, Centre will operate from Monday Kanda Express (trains transporting onions) from Nasik to Delhi, Chennai, Kochi and Guwahati, where prices are higher than the national average.As per consumer affairs department data, the retail price of onion was Rs 65 a kg in Delhi compared with Rs 35 a year back. In Chennai, onion was selling at Rs 58 a kilo as against Rs 33 last year. Onion prices are elevated in parts of Kerala and Assam as well. Retail prices of sugar also continue to rise; on Saturday, it was selling at Rs 62.5 per kg compared with Rs 46 a kilo a month back. In Delhi and Mumbai, retail prices of the sweetener were Rs 65 and Rs 69 a kilo, respectively.On govt intervention to check onion prices, officials said the kitchen staple will be offered at a lower price in a calibrated manner considering that traders may be pushing up prices artificially. They added that there is sufficient stock both with govt and farmers to meet demand in coming months. Food ministry too said there is enough sugar available.The last time govt operated Kanda Express from Nasik to Delhi and other parts of the country to curb rising prices was in Oct 2024.Market insiders said reports of a decline of 5% to 7% in the kharif onion output in Maharashtra, the largest producer among states, have contributed to the rise in prices.Farmers’ cooperative NAFED and National Cooperative Consumers’ Federation (NCCF) have procured around 1.2 lakh tonnes of onion for the current fiscal year as buffer. Earlier in May, these agencies had fixed the procurement price of onion at Rs 1,270 per quintal but revised it to Rs 2,645 last week to accelerate procurement.Onion production in 2025-26 crop year (July-June), according to the second advance estimate of the agriculture ministry, is at 307 lakh tonnes, similar to the production in 2024-25 crop year.Meanwhile, retail prices of loose sugar are on the rise. On Saturday, it was selling at Rs 62.5 per kg, 34% higher than a year back and 28.5% more than a month back.
Article Summary: Average price of the key kitchen commodity increased to Rs 42 per kg on Saturday, 45% higher than last year and 19% more than last month. Centre will operate from Monday Kanda Express (trains transporting onions) from Nasik to Delhi, Chennai, Kochi and Guwahati.

Article Title: Govt to tighten vehicle lighting rules: Low-beam-only bikes, reduced headlamp glare
Article Text:
New vehicle rules may curb high-beam glare, with two-wheelers switching automatically to low beam

NEW DELHI: Automatic headlamps in two-wheelers will soon work only in passing beam (low beam) mode, and buses and other heavy vehicles will have to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather. Also, the use of high-intensity headlamps will be restricted across all categories of vehicles to curb glare, which causes visual discomfort or impairs the vision of other road users.The road transport ministry has proposed these changes, among others, through draft amendments to Central Motor Vehicles Rules, with the new safety norms set to take effect from next April. The amendments in automotive vehicle standards are being made given that efforts to persuade drivers and make them aware of the need to use low-beam mode have not yielded desired results.The automatic headlamp norms would be applicable only for new two-wheelers and not existing ones. At present, the Automatic Headlamp On (AHO) system can switch on both low beam and high beam modes depending on vehicle settings. The proposed rule mandates that when the automatic system is active, the headlamp will be on low beam.As for high-intensity headlamps, the maximum permissible intensity has been reduced from 1.5 lakh candela or cd (official base unit of luminous intensity) to 1 lakh cd for two-wheelers.The maximum permissible intensity for 4-wheelers (cars) has been reduced from 2.25 lakh cd to 1.5 lakh cd.As per studies, white light emitted from headlamps and front fog lamps with higher colour temperatures cause significant glare, leading to discomfort and reduced visibility for other road users. To address this issue, the maximum permissible colour temperature has been restricted to 6,500 Kelvin (K).It has also been proposed that the mounting height of main-beam headlamps be equivalent to that prescribed for passing-beam headlamps.These measures target one of the major causes of night-time road crashes in India — drivers using headlamps on high beam in urban areas, which can temporarily blind motorists approaching from the opposite direction, reducing visibility and increasing the risk of crashes.TOI has learnt that the new-generation system will also include an audio alert to discourage unnecessary use of high-beam mode on city roads. If a driver manually switches to high beam in urban conditions, the vehicle will prompt them to shift back to low beam.However, the alert will be speed sensitive. Drivers travelling on highways at speeds above 60 kmph won’t receive the warning, since the use of high-beam mode may be necessary on poorly illuminated highway stretches. The feature is intended to promote safer driving behaviour in urban areas while ensuring that highway driving is not adversely affected, officials said.The draft amendments also revise lighting requirements across vehicle categories. Besides restricting use of automatic headlamps to low-beam mode, they update norms for high-end headlamps with adaptive passing beam and adaptive high beam.
Article Summary: Automatic headlamps in two-wheelers will soon work only in passing beam (low beam) mode. Buses and other heavy vehicles will have to use genuine reflective tapes to improve visibility at night and in bad weather. Use of high-intensity headlamp will be restricted across all categories of vehicles to curb glare.

Article Title: India set to surpass China in affluent consumers by 2036: Report
Article Text:
India’s affluent consumer base is projected to surge from 2.6 crore in 2026 to 10.8 crore by 2036

India could add 8.2 crore affluent consumers over the next decade, the largest projected increase among major markets





BENGALURU: India is projected to have 10.8 crore affluent consumers by 2036, marginally surpassing China’s 10.3 crore, according to the latest report by NielsenIQ (NIQ) and World Data Lab.The report defines affluent consumers as people spending more than $90 a day, making it a spending category rather than a measure of income or wealth. India is estimated to have about 2.6 crore affluent consumers in 2026 and is projected to add 8.2 crore over the next decade.China is projected to add 6.2 crore affluent consumers during the same period. Among the countries shown separately in the report, India is expected to record the largest increase.The report also estimates that India has 64.9 crore “core consumers” in 2026, defined as people spending between $13 and $90 a day. This is a separate spending group and is not included in the affluent-consumer base.The US is projected to have 23.1 crore affluent consumers by 2036, more than either India or China. Worldwide, the affluent population is forecast to reach 102.5 crore by then, an increase of 36.9 crore from 2026.The 2036 estimates are projections based on available data, historical patterns and assumptions, and actual outcomes could differ, the report said.The report classifies India as a “volume growth” market, citing its rising population and middle class. Its broader observations on growth across product categories, however, apply to emerging markets across Asia-Pacific, Latin America and Africa, rather than specifically to India.“In some categories, growth will be driven by broader household participation, affordability or distribution. In others, it will come from premium purchases as newly affluent consumers look for products that deliver on quality, convenience or status,” the report said.The report’s other consumer findings are also not India-specific. Among people it calls “upgrade consumers”, 60% said they focus on value for money, while 46% said they are willing to pay for convenience. Even consumers willing to spend more may trade down when a premium is unclear or a cheaper product appears sufficient, it added.The findings come after a sharp rise in prices. Global fast-moving consumer goods prices increased 26% between 2021 and 2025, according to NIQ.Affluent consumers represent substantial spending power. In 2026, their global population is estimated at 65.7 crore, against 410 crore core consumers. Yet affluent consumers are projected to spend $35.9 trillion during the year, compared with $31.6 trillion for the much larger core-consumer group.The report said companies will need products that justify an upgrade while retaining affordable options.“The ‘average’ consumer is no longer a reliable growth target,” it said.
Article Summary: India is projected to have 10.8 crore affluent consumers by 2036, marginally surpassing China’s 10.3 crore, according to the latest report. The report defines affluent consumers as people spending more than $90 a day, making it a spending category rather than a measure of income or wealth.

Article Title: India can become global shipbuilding hub: Rajnath after laying foundation of 5 projects in Bengal worth Rs 3500crore
Article Text:
Rajnath, Suvendu Adhikari virtually launch Rs 3,500cr defence expansion projects in Bengal

NEW DELHI: Defence minister Rajnath Singh on Sunday said that India has the capacity to become a global ship design and ship-building hub and must take advantage of the demand-supply gap in the international market. The minister said this while addressing a gathering after he, along with West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, performed the ground-breaking ceremony virtually from Kolkata of five expansion projects of Garden Reach Shipbuilders & Engineers (GRSE) and Yantra India (YIL) that will entail an investment of Rs 3,500 crore. The projects will bolster the nation’s shipbuilding, ship repair, metallurgical and production capabilities, giving a major push towards ‘ Aatmanirbhar Bharat ’ and ‘Make in India’, Make for the World’ initiatives, the defence ministry said.“The demand for ships – naval, cargo vessels or oil tankers – is increasing across the world. On the other hand, in the past few decades, ship manufacturing has reduced in traditional ship manufacturing countries like UK, USA, Netherlands or France. This is a golden period which India can capture,” Rajnath said, adding India has plans to be placed among the top 10 ship-building nations by 2030 and top 5 by 2047 under its Maritime Amrit Kaal Vision 2047.On manufacturing, he said many developed countries are stepping back from labour-intensive shipbuilding due to soaring costs and a shortage of skilled manpower, while India possesses a skilled workforce, a robust steel industry and a strong MSME ecosystem. “If we modernise our manufacturing capacity and adhere to global quality standards, India can emerge as the world’s next major shipbuilding hub,” he said. “Self-reliance is not merely a policy; it is a force multiplier for battlefield capability. In this endeavour, the roles of GRSE and YIL will be crucial,” he said.Rajnath underlined that GRSE’s Raichak facility would provide the capability to build warships up to 200 metres in length and enable the shipyard to bid for next-generation destroyers, while the facilities at Timber Pond in Howrah and the Damodar complex would strengthen the shipbuilding value chain. He said the two forging facilities of YIL would produce high-quality metals for heavy artillery, naval weapons and advanced defence equipment, thereby strengthening the Navy’s operational readiness.Commending GRSE for its efforts to achieve self-reliance in defence manufacturing, Rajnath made special mention of the advanced guided-missile frigate INS Dunagiri, which was dedicated to the nation by PM Modi earlier this year. “GRSE has constructed over 800 vessels to date. Even the next-generation offshore patrol vessels, currently under construction, will feature more than 80% indigenous content. This demonstrates that we are rapidly reducing our dependence on foreign sources,” he said. He described YIL as a strong pillar of India’s defence manufacturing capability, expressing hope that the new modern facilities at the metal and steel factory in Ishapore will fully secure the critical supply chain for advanced weapons and strategic components.Calling maintenance, repair and operations (MRO) a “low-hanging fruit” as it requires neither massive capital investment nor an enormous workforce, the defence minister called for India to establish itself as a hub for ship repair and overhaul in the Indian Ocean Region.Terming the ceremony a “historic moment”, CM Adhikari said the expansion projects will not only enhance the capacities of GRSE and YIL, but also bring about a resurgence in West Bengal’s industrial sector. The projects will generate jobs and provide greater opportunities for ancillary industries, including MSMEs, he added.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh says India has the capacity to become a global ship design and ship-building hub. The minister said this while addressing a gathering after he, along with West Bengal CM Suvendu Adhikari, performed the ground-breaking ceremony virtually from Kolkata. The projects will bolster the nation’s shipbuilding, ship repair, metallurgical and production capabilities.

Article Title: TCS denies employee laptop surveillance reports after monitoring tool claims spark workplace privacy concerns
Article Text:
Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) has reportedly introduced a Digital User Experience Monitoring tool on company-issued laptops, sparking debate over workplace privacy and surveillance. The technology can reportedly track application usage and time spent on devices. While such tools can strengthen cybersecurity, concerns remain over data collection, employee monitoring, access controls and transparency surrounding their use.

Reports of laptop monitoring trigger workplace surveillance concerns

TCS calls surveillance reports ‘baseless and inaccurate’

macro-level network performance

A wider debate over workplace monitoring

Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reportedly deployed a Digital User Experience Monitoring tool on company-issued laptops, triggering questions over whether the technology could be used to monitor employees’ activities. The company has now rejected those reports, calling them “baseless and inaccurate” and stating that it does not track individual employee activity on laptops.The development comes after reports claimed that the monitoring tool could provide visibility into applications accessed on employees’ laptops and the time spent on them. This raised concerns over whether the technology was being used for cybersecurity, network management or monitoring individual work patterns.TCS has now clarified that the tools are intended for a broader technical purpose and are not designed to surveil employees.The initial reports about the deployment of the Digital User Experience Monitoring tool raised questions about how companies use technology to oversee corporate devices.Such tools are increasingly used by organisations to assess the performance of their IT infrastructure, identify technical issues, strengthen security and improve digital services.However, when monitoring software is installed directly on employee devices, concerns can arise over whether it can also capture information about individual users.In the case of TCS, reports suggested that the tool could offer visibility into application usage and the amount of time spent on different applications.That led to a broader question: was the technology intended to monitor the health of TCS' digital infrastructure, or could it also be used to track individual employee behaviour?TCS has now categorically denied that it is using the technology to surveil its employees.In a statement, the company said: “The reports regarding surveillance of employees are baseless and inaccurate. TCS does not track individual employee activity on laptops and respects their privacy.”The company said the tools are used to monitorrather than the activities of individual employees.According to TCS, the purpose is to ensure network security and availability while providing employees with an improved digital experience.The clarification therefore draws a distinction between monitoring the company's technology infrastructure and monitoring the people using it.The episode comes against the backdrop of a wider discussion about digital monitoring at workplaces.As companies increasingly depend on laptops, cloud applications, remote-access systems and digital communication, monitoring the performance and security of these systems has become a routine part of IT management.At the same time, employees are becoming more conscious of the amount of information that workplace technologies can potentially collect.That makes transparency particularly important. Employees need to understand whether a tool is monitoring network health, collecting aggregated technical information or recording individual behaviour.In TCS' case, the company has now said that the technology is used at a macro level and that individual employee activity is not being tracked.
Article Summary: Tata Consultancy Services (TCS) reportedly deployed a Digital User Experience Monitoring tool on company-issued laptops. Reports suggested that the tool could offer visibility into application usage and the amount of time spent on different applications. TCS has now categorically denied that it is using the technology to surveil its employees.

Article Title: Supreme Court cuts judicial service practice rule from 3 years to 1; candidates to undergo training, clerkship after selection
Article Text:
The Supreme Court has reduced the prior legal practice requirement for entry-level judicial service from three years to one year for future recruitment. Selected Civil Judge (Junior Division) candidates will undergo a year of judicial training and another year of supervised clerkship. The ruling also provides transitional relief to law graduates affected by the earlier three-year requirement.

Three-year rule reduced to one year

Transitional relief for law graduates till March 2027

Selection will not mean immediate regular appointment

Two-stage clerkship to give selected candidates courtroom exposure

Why the Supreme Court changed course

Court retains the idea of practical experience

Arrangement can be reviewed after three years

What the ruling means for aspiring judges

The Supreme Court has modified its controversial three-year practice requirement for entry-level judicial service, reducing the mandatory prior legal practice to one year for future recruitment. At the same time, candidates selected as Civil Judges (Junior Division) will have to undergo one year of intensive training followed by one year of structured law clerkship as reported by the Live Law.The decision marks a significant recalibration of the Court's May 2025 judgment, which had restored the requirement of three years of legal practice before law graduates could appear for Civil Judge (Junior Division) examinations. The Court has, however, retained the principle that some practical exposure to the legal profession is necessary before a candidate enters the judiciary.The ruling was delivered by a bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice August George Masih and Justice K Vinod Chandran, who dissented.The Supreme Court has refused to reopen the basic reasoning behind its May 2025 judgment but has substantially altered how the practice requirement will operate.For judicial recruitment notifications issued on or after April 1, 2027, candidates will need to have at least one year of active legal practice before appearing for the Civil Judge (Junior Division) examination. The practice will have to be verified through a certificate, with the Court requiring records of a candidate's presence and participation in effective judicial proceedings.LiveLaw reported that the Chief Justice emphasised that the Court continued to accept the underlying need for professional exposure before a person assumes judicial office. However, the requirement of prior experience must have a reasonable connection with its objective and should not impose disproportionate hardship on aspiring judicial officers.This effectively replaces the three-year threshold with a shorter but more structured route into judicial service.The Court has also created a transition arrangement for candidates caught between the old and new regimes.Law graduates applying under judicial examination notifications issued between May 20, 2025 and March 31, 2027 will be permitted to appear without having completed three years of practice. They will be treated as having completed one year of active practice for the purpose of their applications and will not have to submit a practice certificate for that deemed period.The relief is aimed at candidates who had planned their careers under the earlier system and were suddenly confronted with the restoration of the three-year requirement.The Court observed that the sudden return of the requirement, without a transitional mechanism, had caused hardship to young lawyers and law graduates. LiveLaw quoted the Court as holding that the restoration had "visited hardship" on graduates who had structured their professional lives around the regime that had prevailed for more than two decades.The relaxation in pre-examination practice does not mean that selected candidates will immediately enter regular judicial service.Candidates recruited during the transition period will first be designated as Trainee Judicial Officers. They will have to complete one year of intensive training at the concerned State Judicial Academy. This will be followed by another year of structured law clerkship.The arrangement is designed to shift part of the professional exposure requirement from the period before recruitment to a supervised period after selection.During the academy training, trainees will receive emoluments equivalent to half the gross remuneration of a Judicial Magistrate First Class. During the subsequent clerkship, they will receive the emoluments applicable during their judicial academy training.The post-selection clerkship will itself be divided into two six-month phases. The first six months will be spent working as a law clerk under the supervision of the Principal District Judge or members of the Higher Judicial Service. The remaining six months will be served under the supervision of sitting judges of the concerned High Court.At the end of the clerkship, the supervising High Court judge will submit a reasoned evaluation assessing the trainee's progress and suitability. A satisfactory evaluation will pave the way for appointment to the regular judicial post and the accompanying pay and service benefits.The structure therefore places considerable emphasis on supervised practical learning rather than relying entirely on years spent practising at the Bar.The dispute arose from the Court's May 2025 decision restoring the three-year practice requirement for direct recruitment to the post of Civil Judge (Junior Division).The review petitions argued that the rule could discourage capable law graduates from immediately pursuing judicial service. The concern was particularly sharp because candidates preparing for judicial examinations had already planned their careers under a system that did not require three years of prior practice.During the hearing, counsel opposing the three-year requirement warned of its potential effect on diversity in the judiciary. One submission, quoted by LiveLaw, was: "If you delay by three years, they will not take up this profession. Especially women won't come, persons with disability will not come."Senior Advocate Pinky Anand, according to LiveLaw, argued that the focus should instead be placed on strengthening judicial training after recruitment. She also called for continuing legal education and a more uniform training framework across the country, rather than relying on differing standards followed by individual State Judicial Academies.The judgment does not abandon the principle that future judges need exposure to the legal profession. Instead, the Supreme Court has attempted to balance two competing concerns: ensuring that young judicial officers understand the realities of legal practice while avoiding an unnecessarily long barrier between graduation and entry into judicial service.The Court's approach effectively recognises that practical competence can be developed through a combination of limited prior practice and intensive supervised training after selection.For candidates appearing under the post-April 2027 regime, the route will therefore involve one year of active practice before the examination, one year of judicial academy training after selection and another year of structured clerkship.The Supreme Court has made it clear that the new framework is not necessarily permanent. The Chief Justice observed that the impact of the arrangement should be assessed after it has operated for a reasonable period. The Court has indicated that three years would provide sufficient institutional experience to determine whether the new system is meeting its intended objective.The Court may then revisit the framework based on relevant indicators and its actual functioning on the ground.Justice K Vinod Chandran, however, disagreed with the majority. He recorded his dissent and held that the review petitions should be dismissed.For law graduates aspiring to become Civil Judges, the ruling significantly changes the immediate pathway to judicial service.Those covered by the transition window up to March 31, 2027, will not be required to demonstrate prior practice before appearing for the examination. Those entering the system after April 1, 2027, will face a one-year practice requirement instead of the earlier three-year threshold.But the reduced pre-entry requirement comes with a clear trade-off: Successful candidates will have to undergo substantial supervised professional training after selection.The Supreme Court has thus stopped short of eliminating practical experience from the judicial recruitment process. Instead, it has redesigned the route through which that experience is acquired, reducing the time candidates must spend at the Bar before the examination while strengthening structured exposure after selection.The decision could therefore have a direct bearing on thousands of young law graduates who view the lower judiciary as their first professional destination. It also places a greater responsibility on State Judicial Academies and the higher judiciary to ensure that the promised training and clerkship are rigorous, consistent, and capable of preparing new judicial officers for the demands of the courtroom.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has reduced the mandatory prior legal practice requirement for entry-level judicial service from three years to one year for future recruitment. Selected Civil Judge (Junior Division) candidates will undergo a year of judicial training and another year of supervised clerkship. The ruling also provides transitional relief to law graduates affected by the earlier three-year requirement.

Article Title: Telangana CM Revanth Reddy cuts short trip as Centre nixes nod to visit US
Article Text:
The refusal sparked a major controversy with senior Congress leader and govt whip Adi Srinivas accusing the BJP of politicising even an “education-related tour”.





HYDERABAD: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy was on Friday forced to cut short his two-nation tour to the US and UK after the ministry of external affairs refused him permission to visit the US for an unspecified ‘political angle’.He had left for the UK immediately after attending the Congress Working Committee meeting in New Delhi on Wednesday. He will continue his visit there and return to India seven days earlier on Aug 23.The refusal sparked a major controversy with senior Congress leader and govt whip Adi Srinivas accusing the BJP of politicising even an “education-related tour”.He slammed the saffron party leaders for making baseless allegations against Revanth. BJP MP D Arvind, on the other hand, alleged that the chief minister had proposed to meet representatives of universities who were connected to “anti-national forces”.In a statement from London, Revanth said, “The only purpose of the visit was to, as part of the New Education Policy of the Centre, bring the world’s best institutions to India, to Telangana, to Hyderabad. They would have been an answer to our youth’s aspirations to get education, skills, and training from the best Ivy Leagues and top global institutions.I have always believed we should all think beyond politics and elections when it comes to nation building and the future of the youth. ”The delegation, which includes advisor and ex-officio special chief secretary to CM K Ramakrishna Rao, MCRHRD director general and former chief secretary A Santhi Kumari and Congress leader C Rohin Reddy among others, will now visit the US without Revanth.The plan is to attract managements of top universities and prestigious educational institutions in both countries and urge them to set up campuses in the upcoming Bharat Future City on Hyderabad’s outskirts.After the permission was denied, the chief minister’s office claimed: “The official Telangana Rising delegation led by CM Revanth has been forced to cancel their visit to the United States of America (USA) after the Union external affairs ministry denied permission stating 'clearance' from political angle is denied.”An MEA spokesperson on Friday evening, however, said that the programme proposed for the CM’s US tour was not appropriate, but did not give details.Revanth added, “A single schoo — Hyderabad Public School — has shown how we can lead the world, producing some of the greatest tech leaders (Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, Adobe CEO Shantanu Narayen and World Bank group president are alumni of the school). The starting of IIT, ISB, IIIT, Nalsar helped Hyderabad attract top corporations and their GCCs. Now, we will make Hyderabad the home for the world’s greatest education and skills institutions to power our 21st century journey. ”During his time in the UK, the CM will be interacting with representatives from University of Oxford, University of Cambridge, London School of Economics, the London Business School and University of London, among others.He will also meet with top sports institutions and skilling leadership in the UK.
Article Summary: Telangana chief minister A Revanth Reddy forced to cut short his two-nation tour to the US and UK. Ministry of external affairs refused him permission to visit the US for an unspecified ‘political angle’ He had left for the UK immediately after attending the Congress Working Committee meeting in New Delhi on Wednesday.
